title: 11,000 Accounts Made 25,000 Posts to Unmask Cornell Accuser
summary:
A New York Times analysis has quantified the massive scale of a social media campaign to reveal the identity of a plaintiff alleging she was gang-raped by seven men at Cornell University. More than 11,000 accounts on X, Bluesky, Discord and Telegram published nearly 25,000 posts to identify the woman, referred to as Jane Doe. The data shows the operation persisted across multiple platforms even as Meta and TikTok attempted to limit the spread of content that purported to name her.

A judge sealed the lawsuit on Oct 9 to curb "dangerous internet vigilantism" after misidentified individuals, including a former Marine and several people of Asian descent, were targeted with abuse. The accuser herself has been the subject of repeated swatting attacks, one of which saw police hold her brother and boyfriend at gunpoint. In related court filings, the woman's attorney, Thomas Giuffra, accused defense lawyers of leaking confidential Title IX records to the media, a claim the lawyers have denied.

selectedTweets.bestBit: accusing defense lawyers of selectively leaking confidential Cornell Title IX records to the press
selectedTweets.text:
CORNELL SEVEN LEGAL DRAMA🚨🚨

Here's what unfolded in less than 24 hours:

Wednesday night, Jane Doe’s attorney, Thomas Giuffra, filed a scathing 12-page response accusing defense lawyers of selectively leaking confidential Cornell Title IX records to the press. The filing came as one defendant, Diego Sarabia, sought a court order limiting what attorneys and parties can publicly say about the case. Giuffra strongly opposes that request. Giuffra took shots at TMZ, Mark Geragos, Andrew Miltenberg, Jeremy Saland, Teny Geragos and Tara Davis, criticizing their media involvement and accusing them of leaking evidence to undermine his client. He maintains that his own media appearances were largely in response to leaked evidence and public attacks on Doe's credibility. Giuffra also brought up Sean “Diddy” Combs, drawing comparisons to the publicity surrounding that case and Mark Geragos' media appearances offering a defense perspective, despite not formally representing Combs at trial.

By Thursday morning, attorney Teny Geragos of Agnifilo Intrater, who represents defendant Winston Lee in the related criminal investigation, had fired back. In an email filed with the court, Geragos denied leaking information and demanded that Giuffra publicly retract his allegations by Friday. She warned of potential legal action and instructed him to preserve communications and other records relating to his claims. 

Another filing came in Thursday afternoon.

Attorneys for defendant Diego Sarabia denied providing documents or statements to the media and accused Giuffra of running his own publicity campaign. They cited interviews in which Cornell Daily Sun journalists described communicating with Doe and her lawyers before the lawsuit was filed. They also pointed out that Giuffra referenced Diddy 11 times in his filing, arguing that the unrelated case had no bearing on their request. Sarabia's attorneys maintain that their proposed order would restrict prejudicial public commentary, not prevent anyone from litigating the case in court.

I will have the FULL motions from each lawyer when my story is filed @LAmag
